To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

axo‐axonic interactions between sympathetic and paraspasympathetic neurons in cerebral blood vessels mediate NE transmission and facilitate NO release, which may provide an important mechanism for the control of cerebral blood flow.
NE released from sympathetic nerves acts on β2‐adrenergic receptors on neighbouring parasympthetic nitrergic nerves to enhance NO release with vasodilation.

NE released from sympathetic nerve terminals facilitates NO release from neighbouring parasympthetic nerve terminals via presynaptic β‐adrenoceptors, and that α7‐ and/or α3β2 nAChRs mediate NE release from sympathetic nerve terminals with subsequent nitrergic vasorelaxation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the physiological role of axo‐axo‐axonal interactions in the cerebral circulation, and their relevance to human diseases.
the physiological and pathophysiological role of axo‐axonic interactions in the autonomic regulation of regional cerebral blood flow.
the physiological and pathophysiological roles of axo‐axonic interaction in autonomic cerebral vasomotor control.

NE is not a vasoconstrictor but a vasodilator in the brain, mediated via NO release from the parasympathetics.
axo‐axonic interaction between sympathetic and parapathetic neurones is a major determinant of cerebral blood flow regulation.
NO is the major cerebral vasodilator and NE is the cerebral vasoconstrictor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NE released from the cerebral sympathetic nerve is not only a vasoconstrictor, but also a vasodilator through the axo‐axo‐nitrergic interaction.

the autonomic control of cerebral blood flow is mediated by axo‐axo interaction between nitrergic parasympathetics and sympathetic noradrenergic neurones, and that α7‐ and/or α3β2nAChRs on sympathetic nerve terminals play an important role for the axo‐axal interaction.

the axo‐axo interaction between sympathetic and parapathomimetic nerves in cerebral blood vessels provides a novel mechanism to explain cerebral hypoperfusion associated with Alzheimer’s disease and the limitations of cholinesterase inhibition therapy.

NE transmission is facilitated via axo‐axial interaction between sympathetic and parapathomimetic nerves, leading to enhanced nitrergic vasomotion.
the sympathetic and parapympathetic nervous systems are not antagonistic but synergistic in the cerebral circulation.
the axo‐axo‐nitrergic interaction is a major mechanism for autonomic control of cerebral circulation.
